clue.text: Tax before May on religious centre

indicators.note: the tax word comes first, placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: VAT is value added tax, a British sales tax
'May (I)?' asks permission; read as 'I can'

explanation.surface: A levy on a holy place is announced ahead of the month of May.
explanation.walkthrough: 'May' looks like the month but means 'I can', permission granted.
explanation.definitionFit: Vatican City is the seat of the Roman Catholic Church, a centre of faith.

clue.text: Trying to reach this result

parts.note: trying is read in the courtroom sense, a trial whose outcome is the jury's decision

explanation.surface: Struggling to achieve a particular outcome.
explanation.definitionFit: A verdict is the finding a jury delivers at the end of a trial.

clue.text: Silently, cattily, waywardly

indicators.note: going wayward means straying from order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is quietly spiteful and unpredictable.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacitly means understood without being spoken, without words.

clue.text: Many a fine filament on the seat

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number
a hair is a fine thread-like strand

explanation.surface: Lots of thin threads are left on the sofa.
explanation.definitionFit: A chair is a piece of furniture to sit on.

clue.text: One who counts the top part only

definitions.meaning: a person who numbers or tallies things
the figure above the line in a fraction

explanation.definitionFit: A numerator counts things, and is also the upper number of a fraction above the denominator.

clue.text: Brian was moved during TV broadcast that was thrilling

indicators.note: one piece sits within the span of the other, so it goes inside
broadcast also means scattered, so the two letters of TV are shuffled
a name that was moved has its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Brian's emotional appearance on a television programme was exciting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'TV broadcast' looks like a programme, but 'broadcast' scatters the letters TV into VT; 'was moved' gives IBRAN, which sits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vibrant is full of energy and excitement, so it can be called thrilling.

clue.text: Spring found under the bank

definitions.meaning: to spring is to leap over something
a strongroom in a bank's basement

explanation.definitionFit: To vault is to leap, and a vault is the secure underground strongroom of a bank.

clue.text: Sleeping partner?

parts.note: a sleeping partner is a silent investor, but literally it is someone who shares your bed

explanation.definitionFit: A bedfellow literally shares a bed; a sleeping partner in business takes no active role.

clue.text: A crime wave over a country

indicators.note: in a down clue the shuffled letters sit over, above, the final A
a wave shakes things up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A spate of offences sweeps across a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: America is a common name for the United States, a nation.

clue.text: Willingly departed from this life?

parts.note: willingly is read as 'with a will', describing someone who died leaving a valid will

explanation.surface: Someone who chose to die.
explanation.definitionFit: A testate person has died having made a legal will.

clue.text: It could be a miracle to do this to land

indicators.note: the word could be rearranged into another, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: It would take a miracle to win back some territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Land is reclaimed when marsh or sea is drained and made usable again.

clue.text: Uniform for nudists?

parts.note: a military term for everyday uniform, and a word meaning bare is the natural kit of nudists

explanation.surface: What would a nudist colony wear as its uniform?
explanation.definitionFit: In the forces, 'undress' uniform is ordinary dress as opposed to full ceremonial kit; nudists are naked.

clue.text: Explain another reprint, and in French

indicators.note: another version of the word, rearranged into a new order

parts.note: et is the French for 'and'

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to clarify why a book has another printing and a French edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another reprint' reads as a new edition, but 'another' is the anagram signal giving INTERPR.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to make its meaning clear, to elucidate it.

clue.text: Show girl with inner sex-appeal

indicators.note: the girl's name has another piece as its inner part, placed inside it

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A showgirl is said to have plenty of sex appeal within.
explanation.walkthrough: IT for sex appeal comes from the 1927 film 'It' starring Clara Bow.
explanation.definitionFit: Evita is a stage musical by Lloyd Webber and Rice, a West End show.

clue.text: Herb says licensing hours are over

indicators.note: what someone says is heard, so the spoken word stands in for one spelt differently

parts.note: a British pub landlord calls 'Time!' when legal drinking hours end

explanation.surface: A man called Herb announces that the pub is closing.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, pubs could sell drink only during licensed hours, and the landlord shouts 'Time' at closing.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic plant used in cooking, a common kitchen herb.

clue.text: Ivy possibly always on the go

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
green can mean full of vigour and life, still growing

explanation.surface: A plant called Ivy is perpetually busy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivy keeps its leaves all year round, an example of a plant that never goes bare.

clue.text: One drawer in the gallery might amuse one

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: the Tate is the famous London art gallery
one is the Roman numeral I
a till is a cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: An artist in the Tate's collection might entertain a visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawer' suggests an artist, but here it is the till, the drawer holding cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To titillate is to stimulate or excite pleasantly, much like to entertain or tickle.

clue.text: Best basket is an unnecessary weight on deck

parts.note: top means best, as in 'top quality'
a hamper is a large lidded basket

explanation.surface: The finest picnic basket is just dead weight aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-hamper is nautical for gear above deck that adds weight without use, hence any encumbrance.

clue.text: Not the best cheese for catching vermin

definitions.meaning: a dull, cheap cheddar is jokingly named after what is put out for rodents
a device baited to snare rats and mice

explanation.surface: Inferior cheese is fit only to bait rodents.
explanation.definitionFit: Mousetrap is slang for poor-quality cheese, and also the spring device that catches mice.

clue.text: Graduates spinning coin coming from the lodge

parts.note: MAs are Masters of Arts, university graduates

indicators.note: a spinning coin tumbles, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Former students flip a coin as they leave their club's meeting place.
explanation.definitionFit: Freemasons meet in lodges, so masonic describes things belonging to such a gathering.

clue.text: Public service's usefulness

definitions.meaning: a company supplying gas, water or power
the quality of being practical or of value

explanation.definitionFit: A utility supplies gas, water or electricity to the public, and the word also means practical worth.

clue.text: A charming lady

parts.note: charming is read literally as casting charms or spells, so the lady is a sorceress

explanation.surface: A delightful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch is a woman who casts spells, literally a charmer.

clue.text: Pedro to reconstruct a missile for use in the main

definitions.text: a missile for use in the main

indicators.note: to reconstruct is to rebuild in a new arrangement, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Pedro must rebuild a weapon to be used at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is an old poetic term for the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A torpedo is a self-propelled underwater weapon fired at ships at sea.

clue.text: Crazy type of metal thread?

definitions.meaning: wire used to bind bales of hay

explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means behaving erratically; literally it is the wire used for baling hay.

clue.text: Smart cheat

definitions.meaning: to smart is to hurt with a sharp pain

explanation.definitionFit: A sting is a sharp pain that smarts, and slang for a con or swindle.

clue.text: Is one of its four days of publication December 25 th?

definitions.text: Is one of its four days of publication December 25 th?

parts.words: Is one of its four days of publication December 25 th?
parts.note: Christmas Day is one of the four English quarter days, so a journal issued every quarter might appear then

explanation.surface: A question about whether a magazine comes out on Christmas Day.
explanation.walkthrough: England's quarter days, when rents fell due, are Lady Day, Midsummer, Michaelmas and Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication appearing four times a year comes out every three months.

clue.text: Line of waiters

parts.note: waiters read not as restaurant staff but as people waiting their turn in a row

explanation.surface: A row of restaurant staff.
explanation.definitionFit: A queue is a line of people waiting for something.

clue.text: Times in bars

parts.note: bars read as musical measures, not pubs; the times are the speeds a piece is played at

explanation.surface: Moments spent in pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempi is the plural of tempo, the speed of music measured out across bars.

clue.text: Simplicity of being unusually vain before summer abroad

indicators.note: the shuffled word comes ahead of the next piece
used in an unusual way, the letters are rearranged

parts.note: été is the French word for summer

explanation.surface: It is naive to be vain before a summer holiday overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocent artlessness, a lack of worldly sophistication.

clue.text: Old city ceremony that is in turmoil, I concluded

indicators.note: the I comes last, concluding the word

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial splendour

indicators.note: letters in turmoil are thrown into a new order

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A ceremony descends into chaos and the speaker brings it to an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Nancy performed with energy inside and at the end-hot stuff

indicators.note: the second E is placed last
the letter goes within the shuffled name
performed as in worked over, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Nancy put on an energetic show, and she was hot stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performed' turns NANCY into CAYNN; E goes in after Y and another E is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Cayenne is a fiery red pepper powder, notably hot to the taste.

clue.text: Greeting leading zoologist in the capital found underground

indicators.note: the pieces are placed within the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
hi is an informal greeting

indicators.note: the leading letter, the first one of the word

explanation.surface: A top zoologist is welcomed in the Italian capital on a dig.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhizome is a creeping root-like stem that grows beneath the soil.
